problems.problem: Prose: the plain sense says Chuang Tzŭ “explains his descent”. With only the key verse printed above it, a reader cannot tell that “descent” means naming ever lower things (Tung Kuo Tzŭ’s “Why go so low down?”); it reads as ancestry or a fall, an image left without its point.
problems.fix: Replace “explains his descent” with “defends going so low”: “Having named the ant, a potsherd and ordure to Tung Kuo Tzŭ as places of TAO, Chuang Tzŭ defends going so low; Guo Xiang, on chapter 22, explains that a TAO absent from anything would not reach everywhere, and so would not be TAO.” (44 words, entry-check ok).

problems.problem: Prose: “his work helps things and people give it that name” first reads as helping “things and people”, leaving “give it that name” stranded, and “it” points at the work rather than the Sage. Guo Xiang’s 人與之名 says people give HIM the name.
problems.fix: Read: “...explains that the Sage, like a mirror, has no love, but because his work helps things, people give him that name.” (43 words, entry-check ok).

problems.problem: Prose: “reads the chapter as a man at ease ... humbling himself” says the chapter IS a man; the verb Guo Xiang’s 此篇言 supplies (the chapter says, shows) is missing, so the sentence does not parse cleanly at a first reading.
problems.fix: Insert “showing”: “...reads the chapter as showing one at ease without withdrawing to rivers and seas humbling himself before their recluse, his openness reaching every creature.” (45 words, entry-check ok).
